items.title: Pull-request persistence: a same-request retry after the state branch was pushed is misreported as concurrency-conflict
items.description: Found in PRAXIS-REMOTE-13. In persistence: pull-request mode, scripts/praxis-remote-persist.sh pushes praxis/remote/<digest(requestId)> before gh pr create. If PR creation then fails (rate-limited or repository-write-failed, both advising same-request retry), the retry runs on a fresh checkout, produces a different commit, and pushing it to the existing per-request branch is non-fast-forward, so the adapter reports concurrency-conflict/after-refresh, contradicting the same-request advice. Decide how a retry recognizes and reuses its own existing state branch (e.g. open the PR for it) without force-pushing.

items.title: Grouped-work requirements v2: cross-repository groups, mutation commands, grouped-by-default execution, context and cost measurement (DF-ROS-2026-A053)
items.description: Requirements-only update of requirements/PLANNING-WORK-GROUPS.md on the repository owner's four accepted decisions (session https://claude.ai/code/session_01CmPhre2cFonbHerxVSsmrL): (1) first-class cross-repository groups, (2) group mutation commands and completion semantics, (3) grouped execution as the default for high-affinity groups with enforced reuse-inventory and per-criterion verification gates, (4) context-reuse and cost measurement consumed by the planner. Record decision DF-ROS-2026-A053 amending DF-ROS-2026-A047 (citing EV-ROS-2026-A064, EV-ROS-2026-A070); update docs/planning.md work-group status and required tests; capture follow-on implementation items. Acceptance: new requirement IDs traceable to the decisions; existing IDs stable and amended in place; validate, registry check and tests green; no implementation.

items.title: Group command surface: work group list, idempotent mutations, append-only audit, versioned contracts, derived completion (PRX-GRP-110..116)
items.description: Implement PRX-GRP-110..116 (DF-ROS-2026-A053 decision 2; requirements/PLANNING-WORK-GROUPS.md). Add read-only 'work group list' (filters --status/--member/--repository, sorted); idempotent repeats with changed:false and no history (changes AlreadyMember/NotMember/DuplicateGroup exit 1 -> 0); history entries record the caller's execution ID; validate refuses rewritten/reordered/truncated history; optional work.group.* events; store schemaVersion 2 additive with v1 read unchanged; derived group status vocabulary and removed-open reporting; no group completion transition. Tests: PRX-GRP-190 cases 27-32. Do first: PRAXIS-GROUP-07/09/10 build on it.

items.title: First-class cross-repository groups: GROUP-ECHELON IDs, home record, member references, derived status, cross-repo order (PRX-GRP-100..109)
items.description: Implement PRX-GRP-100..109 and 111's cross-repository rules (DF-ROS-2026-A053 decision 1). Reserved GROUP-ECHELON- prefix; owner/repo:WORK-ID members; homeRepository; 'work group link' writing only an immutable group reference on the member's own item; read-only dated observations of member repositories (fetched ref or remote read) with stale/unknown handling; derived group status; complete/merged/released cross-repo dependency edges and cross-repo cycle detection; per-repository progress; group plan and checkpoints listing per-member repository, branch, checkpoint, PR, observedAt; never write or schedule another repository. Motivating case: portfolio sweeps (one brief, per-repo PRs, consolidated table). Tests: PRX-GRP-190 cases 21-26. After PRAXIS-GROUP-08.

items.title: Grouped-execution completion gates: machine-checkable reuse inventory and per-criterion verification (PRX-GRP-133..135, 040, 045)
items.description: Implement PRX-GRP-133..135 (DF-ROS-2026-A053 decision 3). Schemas praxis.group-analysis/1 (members with enumerated criteria, reuseInventory, searches, newAbstractions) and praxis.group-verification/1 (per member per criterion status and evidence, deferredTo); consumed as work complete --evidence group-analysis=PATH / group-verification=PATH through the DF-ROS-2026-A052 completion-readiness mechanism as a group-verified facet; fail closed, exit 3, no state change; analysis must be committed in an ancestor of the member's first attributed commit; location references must exist. Update docs/group-analysis-template.md with the JSON companion. Tests: PRX-GRP-190 cases 36-37. Must land before PRAXIS-GROUP-09 turns the default on.

items.title: plan execute-group and grouped execution by default for qualifying high-affinity groups (PRX-GRP-117, 130..132, 136..137)
items.description: Implement PRX-GRP-117, 130..132, 136, 137 (DF-ROS-2026-A053 decisions 2-3). plan execute-group records a GEX group execution, begins members in required order via the existing work begin transition with a groupExecution link, never launches agents/branches/providers, idempotent per member, this checkout only. Qualification thresholds under grouping.groupedExecution (high affinity, no none/unknown pair, 2..6 runnable members, same checkout, no limiting context pressure, none captured), shown by plan groups/explain-group; per-group and per-item opt-out with recorded reason; deterministic context-pressure fallback to independent execution. The default takes effect only after PRAXIS-GROUP-10. Tests: PRX-GRP-190 cases 33-35, 38-39, 44. After PRAXIS-GROUP-08 and PRAXIS-GROUP-10.

items.title: Measure context reuse and cost for grouped work and price it in the planner (PRX-GRP-150..158)
items.description: Implement PRX-GRP-150..158 (DF-ROS-2026-A053 decision 4). Provider-neutral context metric capabilities across adapters; time.first_productive_change_ms over configured meaningful paths; context.peak_tokens/window_tokens when exposed; adapter-recorded cost.execution_total where the runtime exposes it and a completion warning when a grouped member lacks cost and capability state; ingest a group execution's shared session once into the GEX; deterministic shared-cost apportionment (direct by member window, group-shared remainder, equal-share 'allocated'); planner pricing of grouped vs independent from >=3 measured samples, else unknown; frozen predicted-vs-observed per GEX. Tests: PRX-GRP-190 cases 40-43. Metric/adapter parts can start now; GEX parts (153, 154, 158) need PRAXIS-GROUP-09.

items.title: Review grouped-by-default at its trigger and roll back if a threshold is crossed (PRX-GRP-138)
items.description: Per PRX-GRP-138 and DF-ROS-2026-A053: after the first 10 grouped-mode executions or 90 days after the default takes effect (whichever first), write an evidence record comparing grouped and independent executions (cost and active time per member, first-pass verification rate, context-pressure fallbacks, 30-day rework) and a decision review. Revert the default to advisory by configuration and a decision record if any rollback trigger holds (grouped median cost per member not lower with >=5 samples each; first-pass verification failure >10 points worse; >1/3 fallbacks; a confirmed attribution-laundering incident caused by grouped mode). Not actionable until PRAXIS-GROUP-09 and PRAXIS-PLAN-10 are complete.

items.title: ORDO-CORE-PACKAGE: consume Ordo.Core as a pinned released package for execution roles, capabilities, mutation-boundary and evaluator semantics (PRX-EXEC-002, PRX-ARCH-001)
items.description: Gap (audit 2026-10-06, rank 7): src/Praxis.Domain/Execution/Governance.fs re-implements Ordo's execution-governance semantics (RoleAuthority.defaultFor, mutation-boundary classification, evaluator fingerprint) and names a backlog item ORDO-CORE-PACKAGE that never existed. Covers PRX-EXEC-002 and PRX-ARCH-001. Prerequisite outside this repository: Ordo publishes Ordo.Core as an immutable release artifact (EchelonFoundry.Ordo.Core nupkg on the Ordo GitHub release, checksummed) through its own PR and workflow_dispatch release. Acceptance criteria: 1. Ordo releases a version whose GitHub release carries the Ordo.Core package with a published sha256. 2. Praxis references that exact version, restored from an immutable, checksum-verified artifact (no floating version, no copied source). 3. Role capability sets come from Ordo.Core (RoleAuthority.defaultFor delegates to Ordo), and no role-to-capability table remains in Praxis. 4. Mutation-boundary classification and evaluator fingerprinting delegate to Ordo.Core. 5. A test fails if the Praxis capability vocabulary and Ordo's diverge, and a test fails if the vendored package does not match its pinned sha256. 6. .echelon/foundations.json and praxis foundations verify evidence the Ordo.Core package pin. 7. Governance.fs header and docs/execution-runtime.md updated; requirement status recorded.

items.title: Accept the mutation boundary and evaluator closure from the governing Ordo execution contract (PRX-BND-001, PRX-SEQ-003, PRX-VER-010)
items.description: Gap: execution start takes the boundary from --scope/--allow and the evaluator from --evaluator CLI flags, not from an Ordo execution contract. Covers PRX-BND-001, PRX-SEQ-003, PRX-VER-010. Depends on PRAXIS-FND-01 (the contract parser is Ordo's). Acceptance criteria: 1. praxis execution start accepts --contract FILE, an ordo.execution-contract/1 document parsed and validated by Ordo.Core, that supplies the role, the semantic mutation boundary (scopes, projections, evaluator references) and the evaluator closure. 2. The envelope records the contract's source path and sha256 so the boundary and evaluator are traceable to the authority that supplied them. 3. Flags that would contradict a supplied contract are refused (exit 2) rather than merged. 4. Without --contract the flags are assembled into the same Ordo contract shape and validated by Ordo, and the envelope records that the operator supplied it. 5. Tests cover contract acceptance, digest recording, invalid contract refusal and flag conflict. 6. docs/execution-runtime.md and requirement status updated.

items.title: Declare Praxis's own shared foundations and make foundations verify evidence them (SAF-DEP-1, SAF-DEP-2)
items.description: Gap: Praxis has no .echelon/foundations.json, so praxis foundations verify cannot evidence its own Aegis, Forma or Ordo use, and the verifier recognises Forma only through package.json (Praxis owns no npm). Covers SAF-DEP-1, SAF-DEP-2. Acceptance criteria: 1. .echelon/foundations.json declares aegis, forma and ordo with their pinned versions, limen and folio as not applicable with the reason recorded in docs/application-foundations.md. 2. aegis-boundaries.json declares every Praxis Aegis boundary code. 3. The verifier accepts a checksum-pinned Forma release-tarball lock and an EchelonFoundry.Ordo.Core PackageReference as pins. 4. A test runs foundations verify against this repository and fails on any finding (systemic guard). 5. requirements status recorded.

items.title: Classify operational failures with Aegis at Praxis's Git, process, filesystem, network and web boundaries, with redaction and sink tests (SAF-AEGIS-1, SAF-AEGIS-5, SAF-AEGIS-6)
items.description: Gap: Aegis is used only as one top-level capture with PRAXIS.CLI.UNHANDLED and an empty scope context (src/Praxis.Cli/Program.fs). Covers SAF-AEGIS-1, 5, 6. Acceptance criteria: 1. One Praxis Aegis boundary module classifies an escaped failure into stable codes per boundary (git, process, filesystem, network, state, web request, unexpected), declared in aegis-boundaries.json and asserted equal by test. 2. The web and hub request handlers capture per request with Aegis and answer 500 with a safe message and reference rather than dropping the connection. 3. Redaction rules extend Aegis defaults for repository URLs, work content, prompts, descriptions and attachment names; a test proves a secret, a token and work content never reach a sink. 4. Tests drive the boundary with a replaceable collector sink: success and refusals record nothing; each boundary code is recorded; programming defects and cancellation are not disguised. 5. Expected outcomes stay typed exit codes (SAF-AEGIS-2 unchanged). 6. Aegis package pin remains a released version.

items.title: Present praxis web serve and hub serve with a pinned Forma release instead of local CSS (SAF-FORMA-1, 2, 5, 6; PRX-UI-030, PRX-UI-031)
items.description: Gap: web/styles.css and web-hub/styles.css are Praxis-local presentation; no Forma release is consumed. Covers SAF-FORMA-1, SAF-FORMA-2, SAF-FORMA-5, SAF-FORMA-6, PRX-UI-030 and the PRX-UI-031 Limen decision. Acceptance criteria: 1. A forma lock pins the immutable Forma release tarball by version, URL and sha256; the tarball is the unmodified release artifact and a test fails if its digest differs. 2. Web and hub serve Forma's dist/all.css from that tarball at a versioned path, and pages link it; local web/styles.css and web-hub/styles.css are removed (no Praxis-local equivalents of Forma presentation). 3. Markup uses Forma classes and patterns (skip link, navigation shell, data/work tables, fields, buttons, status lozenges, alert/fault banners) with native HTML semantics kept. 4. Operational faults and errors render with Forma fault/alert presentation. 5. Tests assert the pinned stylesheet is served, every page links it, no local stylesheet route remains, and key Forma classes are present. 6. PRX-UI-031: record that the script-free server-rendered architecture has no browser runtime for Limen and declare limen not applicable with that reason. 7. docs/web-interface.md and requirement status updated.

items.title: Ingest Tutela security assessments and query security metrics over time with repository, ref and time provenance (TUT-1, TUT-2, TUT-3)
items.description: Gap: Praxis.Domain.Telemetry.Tutela/TutelaTrend are domain-only; nothing ingests or queries them; resolved unknown effects, evidence age and staleness, time-to-expiry, hotspots, boundary/capability changes, remediation lead time and transitions are missing; snapshots have no ref. Covers TUT-1, TUT-2, TUT-3 (TUT-4/5 preserved). Acceptance criteria: 1. praxis tutela ingest --input FILE accepts a Tutela security assessment (schemaVersion 1) and stores an append-only snapshot with repository, ref (the assessment's subject ref, resolved to a commit when it is one), collectedAt and source digest. 2. praxis tutela metrics [--json] projects every listed metric per snapshot and over time: invariant state counts and transitions, unknown effects created and resolved, evidence age and stale evidence, exceptions created/expired and time-to-expiry, recurring/reopened findings, security-sensitive churn and hotspots between snapshot refs, boundary/capability changes, remediation lead time, independent-verification coverage. 3. No single score is produced; output says the metrics are decision support, not certification. 4. A measurement that cannot be derived is reported as unknown, never zero. 5. Tests cover ingest, provenance, each derived metric and missing-as-unknown. 6. docs and requirement status updated.

items.title: Bind an execution envelope to every governed work execution (PRX-EXEC-030, 014, 055, 026, 053, 041)
items.description: Requirements: PRX-EXEC-030, PRX-EXEC-014, PRX-EXEC-055, PRX-EXEC-026, PRX-EXEC-053, PRX-EXEC-041 (requirements/EXECUTION-ORCHESTRATION.md); audit gap 4. Acceptance criteria: (1) work begin/start (also when run by remote execute, and when run in-process by plan execute-group, PRAXIS-GROUP-09) persists .ros/executions/<id>/envelope.json for each begun item, sharing the telemetry execution ID when telemetry is enabled, recording actor, role (default implementation, --role ROLE), baseline HEAD, the current checkout and branch as workspace, and a containment profile; it never creates a branch or worktree. (2) work block/resume/complete/abandon mirror the envelope state with an append-only transition record; complete records the candidate HEAD and the commits baseline..candidate. (3) work resume re-verifies the bound workspace (recorded branch, baseline ancestor of HEAD, recorded candidate ancestor of HEAD) and refuses with exit 3 and no state change on divergence unless --rebind-reason TEXT, which records a rebind event. (4) work complete refuses with exit 3 and no state change while a bound envelope has a mismatched or unknown-effect step receipt or a failed or stale verification. (5) work continue marks the predecessor envelope interrupted and binds the successor with parentExecution. (6) runtime-free fallback reconciliation of work.begin binds an envelope with origin fallback. (7) .ros/executions/** is always-ignored Praxis bookkeeping for attribution. (8) Tests cover each criterion.

items.title: Governed evaluation runner and attributed receipts (PRX-VER-001, 002, PRX-EXEC-024, PRX-REC-007)
items.description: Requirements: PRX-VER-001, PRX-VER-002, PRX-EXEC-024, PRX-REC-007; audit doc discrepancy 'every mutation checks legal actions'. Acceptance criteria: (1) execution start accepts --evaluator-command CMD; execution evaluate runs only the declared command (a different --command is refused, exit 3) and only when the legal action execution.evaluate is available (role holds evaluator.invoke, execution not terminal, evaluator declared). (2) The verification record holds actor id and kind, command identity, candidate commit, evaluator fingerprint, exit code or unknown outcome, and produced evidence references (--evidence PATH). (3) A verification recorded for a different candidate than the workspace HEAD blocks execution.complete as stale. (4) Every step ledger entry Praxis appends carries an attribution (actor/observer id and kind, role, evaluator fingerprint, workspace revision). (5) Every praxis execution mutation is gated by LegalActions; tests cover refusal paths.

items.title: Role-specific launchers and repository execution policy (PRX-EXEC-005, 040, 041, 042, 010)
items.description: Requirements: PRX-EXEC-005, PRX-EXEC-040, PRX-EXEC-041, PRX-EXEC-042, PRX-EXEC-010, PRX-UI-025. Acceptance criteria: (1) ros.json execution.launchers maps roles (optionally a transition) to a configured launcher command; Praxis never selects a provider itself. (2) praxis execution launch EXE-ID [--dry-run] requires the legal action execution.launch, runs the configured launcher for the envelope's role in the workspace with PRAXIS_EXECUTION_ID, PRAXIS_EXECUTION_ROLE, PRAXIS_EXECUTION_ENVELOPE, PRAXIS_WORK_ITEM and the effective capabilities in its environment, and records launcher id, command, exit code and actor. (3) execution start --launch accepts the start first, then launches (UI-025). (4) Separate roles are launchable independently with distinct execution identities; a verification launcher receives only the verification capability set. (5) ros.json execution.worktree (required for listed roles) makes execution start create the worktree automatically. (6) Tests cover each criterion including no-launcher-configured refusal.

items.title: Host containment profile and enforcement evidence (PRX-SEC-001, 003, 010, 011, 013, 014)
items.description: Requirements: PRX-SEC-001, PRX-SEC-003, PRX-SEC-010, PRX-SEC-011, PRX-SEC-013, PRX-SEC-014, PRX-SEC-012 kept. Acceptance criteria: (1) Every envelope carries a containment profile listing filesystem, process, network, credential and environment restrictions, each enforced, unavailable, unrestricted or unknown, with mechanism and evidence; anything the host did not report stays unknown and nothing is inferred from a worktree, branch, directory, prompt or provider permission mode. (2) A host or launcher supplies evidence as praxis.containment-evidence/1 via --containment-evidence FILE or PRAXIS_CONTAINMENT_EVIDENCE; Praxis records its source as host-reported. (3) Containment is host-enforced only when at least one restriction is enforced with evidence; otherwise semantic-only or unknown. (4) Repository policy execution.containment.<role>.require lists restrictions that must be enforced; start and launch refuse (exit 3) when the evidence does not show them. (5) praxis execution containment EXE-ID --json emits the profile in a stable schema documented for Tutela. (6) Tests cover each criterion.

items.title: Local control-plane execution API in web serve (PRX-CTL-001, 003, 005, 006, 011, 012, PRX-UI-008)
items.description: Requirements: PRX-CTL-001, PRX-CTL-003, PRX-CTL-005, PRX-CTL-006, PRX-CTL-011, PRX-CTL-012, PRX-UI-008, PRX-UI-009. Acceptance criteria: (1) GET /api/executions[?workItem=ID] and GET /api/executions/ID return the CLI's own execution JSON (envelope, actor, role, steps with receipt status, scope effects, verification, containment, legalActions with reasons and actorRequirement). (2) POST /api/executions/ID/transitions runs the CLI's own execution transition and returns a structured refusal on an illegal one with state unchanged. (3) GET /api/control-plane declares the bind host, port and whether it is loopback-only. (4) Provider/model/runtime appear only as execution-host attributes of the actor. (5) The host keeps no state and adds no rule: every route shells out to the CLI. (6) Tests cover each route.

items.title: Operator UI execution views with legal actions and human-required boundaries (PRX-UI-001, 004, 007, 020, 021, 026)
items.description: Requirements: PRX-UI-001, PRX-UI-004, PRX-UI-007, PRX-UI-020, PRX-UI-021, PRX-UI-026, PRX-UI-027. Acceptance criteria: (1) The work detail page lists the item's executions with state, role, actor, evaluator and containment. (2) An execution page shows steps with receipt status (match, mismatch, indeterminate, reconciled), unresolved scope effects as obligations, unknown effects, blocked state and verification, each labelled distinctly rather than as a generic failure. (3) Legal actions render with availability, the engine's reasons when unavailable, and a visible human-required marker in text, not color alone. (4) A human-required transition is offered only through a form that records the operator as a human actor with normal provenance; agent/any transitions are separate. (5) The UI computes no legality and has no script. (6) Tests cover each criterion.

items.title: Execution runtime docs and requirement status per row (EXECUTION-ORCHESTRATION status, docs/execution-runtime.md)
items.description: Fix audit documentation discrepancies: docs/execution-runtime.md 'Not yet implemented' points at completed EXEC-INSTALL-109 and claims every mutation checks legal actions; requirements/EXECUTION-ORCHESTRATION.md says Status: Proposed. Acceptance criteria: (1) requirements/EXECUTION-ORCHESTRATION.md carries an accurate status per requirement row (implemented, partial, not implemented, with the work item that covers each gap). (2) docs/execution-runtime.md documents work-transition binding, evaluation runner, launchers, containment evidence, the control-plane API and operator UI, and names open work items for what remains. (3) Untested implemented rows (PRX-EXEC-033, 043, 044, 045, 054) gain tests. (4) A test fails when the requirement status table omits an EXECUTION-ORCHESTRATION requirement ID.

items.title: Consume the Ordo execution contract instead of a local copy of role, boundary and evaluator semantics (PRX-EXEC-002, PRX-ARCH-001, PRX-VER-010, PRX-BND-001, PRX-SEQ-003)
items.description: Gap 7 of the 2026-10-06 audit: src/Praxis.Domain/Execution/Governance.fs copies Ordo's RoleAuthority.defaultFor and evaluator algorithm and refers to a backlog item ORDO-CORE-PACKAGE that does not exist. Acceptance criteria: (1) Praxis takes role capability sets, mutation boundaries and evaluator closure from the governing Ordo execution contract (package or ordo.execution/1 document) rather than CLI flags and a hard-coded matrix. (2) The conformance vectors stay byte-identical. (3) Requirement status rows updated. Depends on Ordo publishing Ordo.Core or an execution-contract document.

items.title: Per-window Stale/Unsupported pacing observation states and hard-hold creation evidence (PRX-QUAL-003, PRX-QUAL-004)
items.description: Covers PRX-QUAL-004 (Stale, Unsupported window states) and the PRX-QUAL-003 creation-evidence gap. Acceptance: 1. WindowStatus has Observed, Missing, Invalid, Stale and Unsupported, each with a stable code in status JSON coverage. 2. A window carried from a cached reading (not in the current response) is Stale, never Observed; a window kind the adapter does not support (unknown Claude limit kind, unknown Codex slot) is Unsupported with a diagnostic, never silently dropped. 3. Stale and Unsupported expected windows make the reading incomplete (freshness stale), with response-shape drift reported as an explicit diagnostic. 4. Hard-limit holds persist creation evidence (observedAt of the triggering reading and the provider window reference) in hold.json as an additive schema-2 field that older readers ignore; holds without it read as unrecorded, never invented. 5. Tests cover each state and the migration.

items.title: Typed provider, model, quota-bucket and scope identities for pacing (PRX-QUAL-005)
items.description: Covers PRX-QUAL-005. Acceptance: 1. ProviderId, ModelId and QuotaBucket are typed values at the Application/Domain boundary; QuotaScope matching uses typed model-family identity with no String.Contains substring matching in policy. 2. Codex Spark bucket selection and Claude scope mapping are explicit, versioned adapter rules (one table each) with fixtures. 3. Unknown models have a declared conservative behaviour: every scoped window applies. 4. Adapter id, rule-set version and capabilities are observable in pacing status (text and JSON). 5. An architecture/guard test refuses Contains-based model matching in the pacing domain and application.

items.title: Typed pacing telemetry events with stable codes replacing free-text pace.log (PRX-QUAL-008)
items.description: Covers PRX-QUAL-008. Acceptance: 1. The gate emits typed PacingEvent values with stable codes: hold-started, hold-retained, hold-released, hard-limit, provider-unavailable, override-enabled, override-disabled, state-fault. 2. Events carry provider, scope, reason kind, reset time and observedAt, never credentials, tokens or raw provider payloads. 3. Repeated polling with an unchanged hold emits no duplicate transition events (deduplicated by transition identity). 4. Events persist as praxis.pacing-event/1 JSON lines (events.jsonl) and pace.log remains as a human-readable rendering of the same events; readers (docs, status) are migrated. 5. Tests cover codes, redaction and deduplication.

items.title: Adversarial pacing adapter tests: Keychain, HTTP errors and redirects, provider process timeout/EOF, live hook fixtures (PRX-QUAL-011)
items.description: Covers the PRX-QUAL-011 cases still missing. Acceptance: 1. Claude credential decoding is testable without a real Keychain: Keychain unavailable, missing entry, expired credential and malformed credential are explicit errors and the snapshot is unavailable, never fresh. 2. The Claude usage query is testable through an injected HTTP handler: a 3xx redirect is refused without following it, 4xx/5xx are explicit errors. 3. The provider process protocol is testable with a scripted stand-in: timeout, EOF before reply, error reply and malformed JSON are explicit errors. 4. Recorded live hook payload fixtures for Claude Code and Codex (PreToolUse and Stop events) drive the gate end to end and produce the provider's documented deny shape. 5. No test uses the live network or a real credential store.

items.title: Provider-neutral capacity port consumed by the planner (PRX-QUAL-009)
items.description: Covers PRX-QUAL-009. Acceptance: 1. A provider-neutral capacity observation (available, constrained until a time, exhausted until a time, unknown with reason) is read by the planner through a port; the planner never calls pacing providers directly. 2. Capacity uncertainty (unknown) is distinct from zero capacity in the plan output. 3. Plan output explains whether capacity affected ordering (a per-item capacity note and a plan-level summary). 4. The planner never proposes switching provider or model; it reports only whether the current provider's capacity constrains the item, and compatibility is out of its authority. 5. Capacity input is optional and read-only: absent capacity leaves plans unchanged. Tests cover all states.

items.title: Declared protocol and state-schema compatibility instead of the release.json == toolchain pin fence (PRX-QUAL-010)
items.description: Covers PRX-QUAL-010. Acceptance: 1. release.json declares the remote protocol range and the state-schema versions this release reads and writes. 2. Repository state declares the state-schema versions it needs; the remote executor refuses a repository whose declared state schema it does not support, before any mutation, with a typed failure. 3. The self-hosting pin may name an older attested release as long as it is compatible with the repository state; source may advance release.json to an unpublished version. 4. The release bump no longer rewrites the pin; a post-release step advances the pin only after the release assets and attestations exist. 5. The equality fence test is replaced by a compatibility fence; tests prove an incompatible executor/state combination is refused before mutation.

items.title: Engineering-risk metadata on work items (PRX-QUAL-020)
items.description: Covers PRX-QUAL-020. Acceptance: 1. A work item may declare praxis.work-risk/1 metadata: change class, risk level, persistent-state impact, external protocol/provider impact, security/privacy impact, failure posture (fail-open, fail-closed, indeterminate), tier ownership and required live/integration proof, set by work capture/update flags and shown by work context. 2. Invalid values are refused at capture/update. 3. Completion obligations (design-debt declaration, verification-matrix dimensions) are derived from the metadata by a pure domain function. 4. Absent metadata keeps existing behaviour. 5. Tests cover parsing, validation and obligation derivation.

items.title: Design-debt declaration as a completion-readiness facet (PRX-QUAL-021)
items.description: Covers PRX-QUAL-021. Acceptance: 1. Completion accepts --evidence design-debt=PATH, a praxis.design-debt/1 document declaring either no known design debt or debt entries referencing captured work items with rationale, risk and the compromised boundary. 2. A design-debt-declared facet joins the A052 completion-readiness record. 3. For high-risk work (from PRAXIS-QUAL-07 metadata), a missing declaration or debt referencing no recorded non-terminal work item refuses completion (exit 3, no state change). 4. A declared prototype cannot complete as canonical without a debt entry. 5. Tests cover each case.

items.title: Verification-matrix obligation as a completion-readiness facet (PRX-QUAL-022)
items.description: Covers PRX-QUAL-022. Acceptance: 1. Completion accepts --evidence verification-matrix=PATH, a praxis.verification-matrix/1 document with rows for happy path, negative/failure, corruption/partial state, concurrency, compatibility/version skew, recovery/rollback and representative live effect, each met, not-applicable (with reason) or not-met, with evidence. 2. A verification-matrix facet joins the A052 completion-readiness record. 3. For stateful control-plane, persistence, release/bootstrap, security or remote-execution work (from PRAXIS-QUAL-07 change class), a missing matrix or any required dimension not met refuses completion; unit-test or build evidence alone never satisfies it. 4. Tests cover each case.

items.title: Input-document inbox: crash-safe claim/process lifecycle with provenance-preserving derivation (DER-09, DER-10)
items.description: Covers requirements/PRAXIS-DUAL-ENTRY-RECONCILIATION.md items 9 and 10 (DER-09, DER-10) and its acceptance criterion 'Inbox claim/retry/reconcile tests prove no source is lost'. Today only 'praxis inbox list' exists and .praxis/processing is unused. Acceptance criteria: (1) 'praxis inbox claim PATH' moves an input from .praxis/inbox/documents (or legacy input-documents) into .praxis/processing/<claim-id>/ with a praxis.inbox-claim/1 record holding the source path, SHA-256 digest, size, claimant identity, execution and claim time; the source bytes are never modified. (2) Claiming is crash-safe and idempotent: the claim record is written before the source moves, a repeated claim of the same digest returns the existing claim, and a claim interrupted at any step is detected and completed or rolled back by 'praxis inbox recover' without losing or duplicating the source. (3) 'praxis inbox derive CLAIM-ID --kind requirement|decision|constraint|evidence|risk|question|reference --id ID|--path PATH --summary TEXT' records each derived canonical artifact with provenance back to the input (claim ID, source path and digest, excerpt locator); classification stays advisory. (4) 'praxis inbox complete CLAIM-ID' refuses while any derived artifact is missing from the working tree or not committed in HEAD (not durably reconciled), and only then archives the input with its provenance record; 'praxis inbox release CLAIM-ID --reason' returns an unfinished claim to the inbox. (5) Rejected inputs move to .praxis/rejected with a machine-readable reason. (6) 'inbox list' reports pending, claimed and rejected inputs and still works without a runtime by reading the directories. (7) Tests: claim/derive/complete happy path; crash after claim record but before move, after move but before completion, and during completion, each recovered with no source lost or duplicated; idempotent repeated claim; completion refused before commit; release; reject. (8) docs/fallback-reconciliation.md, the inbox README and docs/cli.md describe the lifecycle; the DER status in docs is updated.

items.title: Planner: observe CI status for checkpoints that wait on CI (PRX-PLAN-020)
items.description: Covers PRX-PLAN-020 (and PLAN-021's labelling). Merged PRs and release tags are already Git-observed; CI is only taken from a supplied --observations file. items.title: Planner replay: compare predicted and observed cost (PRX-PLAN-152)

items.title: Planner: compare a saved plan's recommendations with what happened (PRX-PLAN-162)

items.title: Record the cross-provider continuation proof on main (RQ-ROS-2026-A023 acceptance, PRAXIS-XPROVIDER-PROOF-01)

items.title: Typed repository identity and canonical work-item identity (PRX-REMOTE-045, 046, 048, 049, 050)
items.description: Close PRX-REMOTE-045, 046, 048, 049 and 050 (GitHub issue #90, adopted by RQ-ROS-2026-A021) and the Contradicted rule that ros.json repository.id is only a name. Acceptance criteria: (1) the domain has typed RepositoryIdentity (provider, stable provider ID, owner/repo locator) and WorkItemIdentity (repository + local ID) values; the display form owner/repo:ID is derived and never parsed to establish identity; (2) the same local ID in two repositories, and two repositories with the same name under different owners, are distinct identities; a rename or transfer (same provider ID, new locator) keeps the identity; (3) an unqualified ID resolves only inside one repository context, and an unqualified lookup across several repositories that is ambiguous fails closed; (4) duplicate or conflicting canonical identities (one provider ID with two locators in one observation, one locator claimed by two provider IDs) fail closed; (5) ros.json gains a versioned repository.identity {provider, providerId, locator}; the legacy repository.id name is kept, read, and reported explicitly as legacy; 'praxis repository identity' shows and sets it and verifies it against the hosting platform's observed ID (GITHUB_REPOSITORY_ID) when available; validate reports a legacy or locator-changed identity as a warning and a contradicted one as an error, while a never-adopted identity is reported by 'praxis repository identity' and 'work capture' rather than as a validate warning on every repository (decision recorded in the group verification); the migration rule is documented; (6) work capture reports the canonical identity, or states that it is incomplete because the repository identity is not established; (7) the structured reference {repositoryId, repository, localId} round-trips through JSON without parsing the display string; (8) tests cover every PRX-REMOTE-050 case. Reuse: Target.repositoryFromRemote (Domain/Installation/Registration.fs) and the owner/repo:ID grammar used by PRAXIS-GROUP-07 member references.

items.title: Remote protocol 1.4: structured canonical work-item references with explicit old-peer compatibility (PRX-REMOTE-047, implementation-order amendment)
items.description: The remote protocol must consume the canonical identity model of PRAXIS-ID-01 instead of bare workItemId/workItemIds strings (PRX-REMOTE-047 and the issue #90 implementation-order amendment). Acceptance criteria: (1) protocol 1.4 accepts {repositoryId, repository, localId} objects wherever a work-item ID is accepted, including batch constituents; (2) a bare ID stays valid and means the executing repository; (3) a structured reference naming another repository, or one whose provider ID and locator contradict the executing repository, is refused fail-closed with invalid-request and changes nothing; (4) a structured reference in a 1.0-1.3 request is refused as invalid; a 1.4 request to a 1.3 executor is refused as unsupported-protocol by the existing rule; 1.0-1.3 requests behave and fingerprint exactly as before, so recorded replays still match; (5) praxis.describe advertises the executing repository's identity and the reference shape; responses carry the canonical identity of the work items they acted on; (6) docs/remote-protocol.md and docs/remote-agent-contract.md document the shape, compatibility and refusal rules; (7) tests cover each case. Depends on PRAXIS-ID-01.

items.title: Telemetry and planner schemas carry canonical work-item identity; correct identity status docs (PRX-REMOTE-047, PRX-PLAN-182)

Acceptance criteria: (1) new execution telemetry records carry workItem {repositoryId, repository, localId} next to the legacy workItemId, and records without it stay valid (legacy rule documented); (2) every praxis.plan document carries the repository identity it was computed in, so each work-item ID in it is the local ID of a canonical identity in that repository, with no competing identity scheme (PRX-PLAN-182); parsers read documents without it (per-item references were not added: the document-level identity qualifies every local ID and keeps the plan schema the grouped-work track is extending stable); (3) docs/planning.md no longer reports PRX-PLAN-182 as met on the grounds that no identity scheme exists; (4) RQ-ROS-2026-A021 names PRX-REMOTE-001..050, no longer defers the npm bin to the abandoned PRAXIS-NPM-BIN and no longer cites deleted Node test files; (5) tests cover the round-trips. Depends on PRAXIS-ID-01.

items.title: Generate and govern the Praxis instance identity (DER-16, 17, 22, 23, 24)
items.description: requirements/PRAXIS-DUAL-ENTRY-RECONCILIATION.md items 16, 17, 22, 23 and 24 (audit IDs DER-16/17/22/23/24): no code generates .praxis/instance.json, so instance-mismatch rejection is inert. Acceptance criteria: (1) praxis init, praxis upgrade and an explicit 'praxis instance init' create .praxis/instance.json (schema praxis.instance/1, a random instance ID, createdAt, the Praxis version and the repository it was created for) before any registration is attempted, and never replace an existing one; (2) an upgrade preserves the instance ID; (3) a clone of the same repository keeps the identity; a copy into another repository (template or fork, detected from the stable provider ID) is reported as foreign, is never stamped into new telemetry and is refused by envelope reconciliation until 'praxis instance init --reinitialize --reason TEXT' creates a new identity that records its predecessor; a rename or transfer keeps it; (4) new telemetry executions and envelope receipts carry the local instance ID; (5) envelope reconciliation rejects a claimed instance ID that differs from the generated local one, proved end to end with an instance file created by the generator; (6) the instance reader reports a malformed file as a typed failure instead of swallowing the exception; (7) validate reports a missing or foreign instance identity; (8) this repository gets its own instance identity. Tests prove each criterion.

items.title: Praxis instance registration projection (DER-19, 20, 25, 26)
items.description: requirements/PRAXIS-DUAL-ENTRY-RECONCILIATION.md items 19, 20, 25 and 26: installation register records system installations, not an instance identity projection. Acceptance criteria: (1) 'praxis instance projection [--json]' renders a praxis.instance-projection/1 document with the instance ID, repository/provider coordinates, Praxis version, reconciliation and remote protocol versions, supported capabilities and the availability state of each optional Echelon integration, where unknown and unavailable are representable and are not failures; (2) it works with no Echelon component, network or credentials; (3) 'praxis instance register' sends the projection through the existing installation registration client with a deterministic operation ID, so a retry is idempotent and never creates a second identity; an unavailable registry exits 0 and changes nothing local; (4) the projection is built from an allow-list and contains no credentials, secrets, local paths or agent-private data, proved by a test that seeds secrets in the environment and configuration. Depends on PRAXIS-ID-04.

items.title: Policy-gated validate rule: meaningful work runs on a branch named for its work item (DER-01)
items.description: requirements/PRAXIS-DUAL-ENTRY-RECONCILIATION.md item 1 and its acceptance criterion 'Validation rejects meaningful work on a branch other than its work-item ID'. Today only the envelope path enforces it. Acceptance criteria: (1) ros.json workProtocol.branchPolicy 'work-item-id' enables the rule; it is off by default and the setting is validated; (2) with the policy on, praxis validate reports an error when meaningful changes (working tree plus ROS_BASE_REF range) exist on a branch whose name is not the ID of a work item recorded in the work context; (3) the branch is read from GITHUB_HEAD_REF in pull-request CI and from Git otherwise; an unknown or detached branch with meaningful work is an error, not a pass; (4) no meaningful changes, or the policy off, produce no finding; (5) the decision is a pure domain rule with unit tests, and an integration test runs validate on a real repository for both outcomes; (6) docs/work-protocol.md documents the setting.
